turns.prompt:
You are given two attached CSV files describing perovskite solar cells as
complete devices — `substrate` (glass + transparent electrode), `etl`
(electron-transport layer stack), `htl` (hole-transport layer stack),
`backcontact` (metal / carbon back electrode), `deposition` (absorber
deposition procedure; `>>` separates steps). Every candidate below uses the
same MAPbI3 absorber in the same p-i-n (inverted) architecture; they differ
only in the remaining columns. Each row is a device CONFIGURATION whose
efficiency is the median over at least 3 independently fabricated cells, so
it is a reproducible recipe rather than a single champion cell:
  - b3_pvk_stack_pin_train.csv: 300 configurations with the measured power
    conversion efficiency (%).
  - b3_pvk_stack_pin_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE configurations whose power
    conversion efficiency (%) was NOT measured, columns `candidate_id` and
    the same device columns.

Using the training data, select the 5 candidates with the HIGHEST power
conversion efficiency (%).

Reason from the device physics — band alignment and selectivity of the
transport layers, interface recombination, contact chemistry and the film
quality the process is likely to give — then end your answer with an
explicit ranked list of candidate_ids, best first, e.g. "Final: c901, c902,
c903, c904, c905".
turns.answer_text:
# Reasoning from device physics

For p-i-n MAPbI3, the top-performing training configs share clear patterns. Let me identify the winning "signatures":

**Highest-efficiency motifs in training data (>18%):**
- `C60 | BCP` or `PCBM-60 | BCP` electron stack (BCP dipole/buffer improves selectivity, cuts interface recombination) → repeatedly 17–19%
- **PTAA HTL** on ITO with **Cu** back contact (PTAA is well band-aligned to MAPbI3 VBM, low recombination; Cu gives good ohmic contact & less halide reaction than Ag): 18.62, 18.85, 19.085
- **NiO-c** engineered with dipole/passivation interlayers (SDBS, SY, [BMIM]BF4, Au-np): 19.04, 20.0, 21.33
- Clean `C60 | BCP` with NiO-np: 17.8–19.7

**Losing motifs:** bare PEDOT:PSS (work-function too shallow → Voc loss, but note the one 24.8 outlier is anomalous), ZnO in contact with perovskite, Cu2O/CuO absorber-degrading oxides, flexible/plastic substrates (lower film quality), exotic single-molecule ETLs.

## Screening the pool for the winning signatures

- **c044** `PCBM-60 | BCP → PTAA → Cu`: exact match to the 18.6–19.1% champions (BCP buffer + PTAA + Cu). **Top pick.**
- **c088** `C60 | BCP → PTAA → Cu` (Willow glass): matches 18.62/19.085% signature; substrate is rigid glass-like, minor penalty.
- **c085** `TTC | C60 | BCP → PTAA → Ag`: C60|BCP + PTAA, with a passivating TTC interlayer (SAM-type, boosts selectivity) → strong, ~17.3–18%.
- **c035** `TEAI | PCBM-60 | PEI → NiO-c → Ag`: NiO-c with TEAI passivation + PEI dipole — mirrors the top NiO passivation family (15.3, and higher with additives). Solid.
- **c041** `PCBM-60 | BCP → NiMgLiO-c → Ag`: Li/Mg-doped NiO gives best NiO-class results in training (18.185 NiMgLiO), plus BCP buffer.
- **c066** `TEABr | PCBM-60 | PEI → NiO-c → Ag`: same passivated NiO family as the 15.3% row.
- **c009** `C60 | BCP → NiO-c → Ag`: clean canonical stack (~14.3–15% class).

The PTAA+Cu with BCP buffer combos are the standout physics (best band alignment + stable contact + passivated ETL interface), so they rank highest. Doped-NiO and passivated-NiO with dipole layers follow.

## Final ranking

Best picks: c044 and c088 (BCP+PTAA+Cu champions), c085 (SAM-passivated C60/BCP + PTAA), c041 (Li-doped NiO + BCP), c035 (TEAI/PEI passivated NiO).

Final: c044, c088, c085, c041, c035
